title: Lie-Algebraic Classical Simulation of Bosonic Systems Beyond Gaussian Dynamics
authors: Adelina Bärligea, Timothy Heightman, Jakob S. Kottmann, Antonio Acín
abstract: Classical simulability is ultimately determined by both the dynamics of a quantum system and the observables being evaluated. Lie-algebraic simulation exploits the latter to make exact polynomial-time classical simulations by propagating observables through low-dimensional invariant operator spaces. However, its conventional formulation in terms of polynomial-dimensional dynamical Lie algebras does not directly accommodate bosonic systems as their algebras are neither compact nor semisimple. In this contribution, we overcome this limitation, making bosonic systems accessible to the Lie-algebraic programme of exact polynomial-time classical simulation. We prove that expectation values, fixed-order correlation functions, including multi-time correlators and out-of-time-ordered correlators, and gradients are efficiently computable whenever their operator modules have polynomial dimension. This recovers Gaussian quantum optics and extends it to non-Gaussian input states, while identifying exact polynomial regimes of interacting non-Gaussian dynamics including bounded-photon Kerr and pair-hopping Hamiltonians and nilpotent polynomial phase dynamics. We show that unlike in the finite-dimensional spin and fermionic setting treated previously, a finite-dimensional bosonic generator algebra alone does not guarantee finite observable dynamics. We further derive a controlled perturbative hierarchy for squeezing beyond exact sector confinement and confirm the predicted error orders numerically. We also evaluate operator spreading on interacting chains of up to $400$ modes and connect a topological doublon band with flux-reversed edge motion. These results provide a unified formalism for classifying, discovering, and systematically approximating tractable bosonic quantum dynamics with classical polynomial-time simulation.
summary: This paper extends Lie-algebraic simulation techniques to bosonic systems, overcoming previous limitations that restricted the method to Gaussian dynamics. By focusing on the finite-dimensional subspace spanned by observables (the reachable module), the authors prove that many non-Gaussian bosonic dynamics can be simulated exactly in polynomial time. This provides a general tool for classifying and approximating tractable quantum dynamics in photonics and condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of developing an exact, polynomial-time classical simulation method for bosonic quantum systems that goes beyond the limitations of standard Gaussian dynamics.
main_result: The authors establish a unified formalism showing that exact simulation is possible for many non-Gaussian bosonic dynamics by restricting the computation to the finite-dimensional, observable-seeded reachable operator module.
method: The core method involves leveraging Lie-algebraic simulation by propagating observables through the invariant operator space defined by the system's generators, rather than simulating the full state evolution.
model_or_system: The focus is on bosonic systems (e.g., photons, phonons) described by infinite-dimensional Fock spaces, extending applicability to interacting non-Gaussian Hamiltonians like Kerr and pair-hopping terms.
key_observables: Expectation values, fixed-order correlation functions (including multi-time and OTOCs), and parameter gradients are shown to be efficiently computable.
important_parameters: The key parameter is the polynomial dimension of the observable's reachable operator module, which dictates the tractability of the simulation.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the relevant observable module has a finite, polynomial dimension, allowing the infinite-dimensional dynamics to be contracted into a finite matrix representation.
figures_summary: The notes describe a workflow illustrating the observable-seeded construction of the reachable operator module, showing how mean values are propagated backwards and how the adjoint action generates the invariant module.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the failure of conventional Lie-algebraic methods for bosons, then introduces the observable-seeded reachable module, and finally demonstrates its applicability across three regimes: quadratic dynamics, U(1) symmetry sectors, and nilpotent phase families.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, systematic theoretical framework for determining the classical simulability boundary for complex, non-Gaussian bosonic quantum dynamics, which is crucial for quantum optics and quantum simulation.
